author: Nancy Burns-Fusaro Sun staff writer
title: 'Thriller Panel' at Ocean House to include Westerly native Christa Carmen
text:
WESTERLY — Westerly's own Christa Carmen will join fellow authors Deborah Goodrich Royce, Karen Dukess, Vanessa Lillie, Kristin Offiler and Tessa Wegert Sunday at Ocean House for the annual "Thriller Panel" an event described as "an engaging conversation about writing, suspense, and storytelling that brings together "some of the most compelling thriller writers in the region.
The event will be moderated by Goodrich Royce, author of "Finding Mrs. Ford," "Ruby Falls," and "Reef Road," and will offer readers a chance to connect with their favorite authors in an intimate and inspiring setting.
Each author plans to discuss one "featured book."
Christa Carmen, the Bram Stoker Award-winning and two-time Shirley Jackson Award-nominated author of "The Daughters of Block Island," and "Beneath the Poet's House," will talk mostly about her featured book, her forthcoming "How to Fake a Haunting," set to be released later this month.
Lillie is the USA Today bestselling author of "Blood Sisters," a new series centered on the stories of "Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls," which was a Target Book Club pick and GMA Book Club Buzz Pick, as well as a best mystery of the year from the Washington Post, Amazon Editor’s and Reader’s Digest.
The sequel, "The Bone Thief," is set to be released on Oct. 28th. Lillie's other bestselling thrillers include "Little Voices, For the Best." She is also the creator and co-author of the "Young Rich Widows" series which is set in Providence and is a "Number One Audible Charts" bestseller and an International Thriller Writers award nominee. Originally from Miami, Oklahoma, Lillie now lives in Providence and is a proud citizen of the Cherokee Nation.
Dukess, the author of "The Last Book Party" and "Welcome to Murder Week," plans to discuss her featured book, "Welcome to Murder Week." She is a former newspaper reporter in Florida, magazine publisher in Russia, and speechwriter on gender equality for the United Nations. Dukess lives in New York and Truro, where she interviews some of today’s most acclaimed writers as host of the Castle Hill Author Talks for the Truro Center for the Arts.
Offiler's short fiction has appeared in the Raleigh Review, Waccamaw Journal, The Bookends Review, and The Bookends Review Best of 2020 print anthology. When she’s not writing, she can be found reading on the porch of her 130-year-old house or exploring charming corners of New England. She lives in Rhode Island with her husband, son, and dog. Her featured book is "The Housewarming."
Wegert is the author of the Shana Merchant series of mysteries. A former freelance journalist, Wegert has contributed to such publications as Forbes, The Huffington Post, Adweek, The Economist, and The Globe and Mail. She grew up in Quebec and now lives with her husband and children in Connecticut, where she studies martial arts and is currently at work on her next novel. Her featured book is "In the Bones."
Following the discussion, guests will have the opportunity to meet the authors and have their books signed. Tickets also include a copy of one featured book of your choice, with other titles available for purchase from Martin House Books during the event.
